title: Google search biggest update in 25 years
description:
Google called this the biggest upgrade to the Search box in 25 years. The reaction was immediate.

DuckDuckGo US install spike peaked at 30.5% week-over-week on May 25. iOS installs peaked at 69.9%. Traffic to noai.duckduckgo.com, which strips every AI feature from results, averaged 22.7% WoW growth. DuckDuckGo's own figures, independently corroborated by analytics firm Apptopia: 29% increase in average daily US downloads over the same period.

Duck.ai runs on Claude 4.5 Haiku, Llama 4 Scout, Mistral Small 3 24B, and GPT-5 mini. IP is stripped before requests reach any model provider. Conversations deleted within 30 days. Nothing used for training. Free, no account required.

DuckDuckGo's CEO testified during Google's 2023 antitrust trial that Google's exclusive default search contracts with browsers and device manufacturers limited DDG's ability to compete at the point where people actually set their preferences. The install spike this week is the same structural problem playing out in a different form.

Google notes that AI Mode is not the default tab and a web filter option exists for plain link results. Whether that counts as a real opt-out is a product design question worth sitting with.

Out of that billion monthly users, how many were actually looking for AI search?
